'''Nancy Ann Neudauer''' is an American mathematician specializing in [[matroid theory]] and known for her work in mathematical outreach in Africa and South America. She is a professor of mathematics at [[Pacific University]],{{r|stereo}} a co-director of the [[Center for Undergraduate Research in Mathematics]],{{r|curm}} and a former governor of the Pacific Northwest Section of the [[Mathematical Association of America]].{{r|gov}}

==Education==
Neudauer grew up in [[Milwaukee]].{{r|stereo}} She was an undergraduate business student at the [[University of Wisconsin]], where she graduated with a double major in [[actuarial science]] and in Wisconsin's program in risk management and insurance.{{r|profile|stereo}} After originally planning to go from there to law school,{{r|stereo}} she stayed at Wisconsin for a master's degree and PhD in mathematics.{{r|profile}} Her 1998 doctoral dissertation, ''The Transversal Presentations and Graphs of Bicircular Matroids'', was supervised by [[Richard A. Brualdi]].{{r|mgp}}

==Service==
Neudauer has been funded by the [[Simons Foundation]], and multiple times by the [[Fulbright Program]], to promote mathematics in Africa and South America by traveling there to teach students graduate-level mathematics, with the goal of better preparing them for graduate study abroad.{{r|stereo|olive|aims|4f|cont}} Her work in Africa has also included helping to develop support networks for women in mathematics there.{{r|4w}}

Neudauer was governor of the Pacific Northwest Section of the [[Mathematical Association of America]] from 2006 to 2009.{{r|gov}} She is a co-director of the [[Center for Undergraduate Research in Mathematics]].{{r|curm}}

==Outreach==

Neudauer is known for her outreach work across America and Africa, receiving multiple Fulbright awards for her work supporting the [[African Institute for Mathematical Sciences]].{{r|einstein}}

==Recognition==
In 2010 the Pacific Northwest Section gave Neudauer their annual Award for Distinguished College or University Teaching of Mathematics.{{r|teach}} She was named as a Fellow of the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]], in the 2027 class of fellows, "for her far-reaching mentoring from the Global South to the Pacific Northwest which has influenced generations of women mathematicians".{{r|fawm}}
